styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Trinity, the Castle, cathedrals and Kilmainham Gaol.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, literary pubs and Georgian streets.

styles.label: Nightlife
styles.blurb: Temple Bar pints, live music and late bars.

stays.why: Central and walkable to Trinity, the Castle and the river. Noisy at night and the priciest per square metre.
Quiet Georgian streets near Merrion Square and the National Gallery; good for couples and longer stays.
Modern hotels, often better value, near the Luas Red line and the 3Arena; a 15–20 minute walk to the centre.
Local neighbourhood with cafés and pubs; cheaper rooms, but you bus or Luas into the centre.

food: Try a full Irish breakfast, then coddle or Irish stew in a traditional pub; lunch mains often €12–18.
Seafood chowder and fish and chips are the safe bets; check the catch of the day on the board.
Book dinner ahead for Friday and Saturday; popular places in the centre fill up.
Cheap eats: chip shops, bakeries and market stalls around €6–12 a meal.
Pints cost roughly €6–8 in the centre, more in Temple Bar. Check for a live-music cover charge.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for Howth: DART train to the harbour, cliff walk and seafood lunch.
History fans can add a day trip to Glendalough in the Wicklow Mountains; check bus tours and times on the day.
Add a distillery or brewery tour (Jameson, Guinness Storehouse) — book a slot online to skip queues.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Trinity, the Castle, a cathedral and a museum, with one evening of pubs and live music.

month_notes: Cold and damp: highs near 8°C, rain on about 12 days. Pack a warm waterproof coat.
Similar to January: 9°C highs, 13 rain days. Indoor sights are the plan.
Still cool at 10°C with 14 rain days; expect showers most weeks.
Milder at 12°C, 12 rain days. Good for walking the centre.
Warmer: 15°C highs, 9°C nights, 12 rain days. Parks and day trips open up.
Long bright evenings, 18°C highs, 13 rain days. Bring a light rain layer anyway.
Warmest month: 19°C highs, 15 rain days. Busy tourist season; book ahead.
Warm at 19°C with 14 rain days. Showers pass quickly; keep plans flexible.
Cooling to 17°C, 13 rain days. Pleasant for walking and outdoor sights.
Autumn: 14°C highs, 14 rain days. Layers and an umbrella.
Cooler at 11°C, 13 rain days. Fewer crowds, shorter days.
Cold and wet: 9°C highs, 15 rain days. Dark by late afternoon; plan indoor evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Mild, changeable and often wet: rain on roughly 12–15 days every month, and rarely very hot or very cold.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Expect rain on about 12–15 days each month. Showers are often short; carry a compact waterproof.

items.title: Pack layers
items.text: Highs run from about 8°C in winter to 19°C in summer. A warm mid-layer and a rain jacket cover most trips.

items.title: Best months: May to September
items.text: Warmest and brightest, with highs of 15–19°C. Still bring rain gear — wet days happen.

items.title: Winter is cool, not freezing
items.text: January and February sit around 8–9°C by day and 4°C at night. Wind off the river feels colder.

items.title: Long summer evenings
items.text: June and July give the longest daylight, good for late walks and outdoor pints.

items.title: Wear comfortable shoes
items.text: You will walk a lot on cobbles and wet pavements. Waterproof shoes beat an umbrella in wind.

transit.best: Walk the compact centre; use the Luas tram or buses for longer hops.

modes.text: Luas has two lines, Red and Green, across the centre. Flat €2 adult fare with a Leap Card.
Dublin Bus and Go-Ahead cover most of the city. Pay exact coins or use a Leap Card (€2 flat fare, daily caps apply).
Metered taxis; Free Now and Uber work in Dublin. Handy for late nights and the airport.
Heavy traffic and limited parking. Use Park & Ride at Luas or DART stops instead of driving in.
The centre is compact and best on foot. Dublinbikes stations are widely spread for longer rides.
